designSpec: A six-point attendance trend with a visible takeaway and an exact-count alternative.
template:
<Card size="md" gap={4}>
  <Col gap={1}>
    <Caption value={demoNote} />
    <Title value={title} size="sm" />
    <Text value={takeaway} size="sm" />
  </Col>
  <SegmentedControl name="view" ariaLabel={viewLabel} options={views} value={view} size="lg"
    $onChangeAction='{ updateState: { view: value } }' />
  <Show $when="view === 'chart'">
    <Col gap={1}>
      <Caption value={axisNote} />
      <LineChart data={sessions} xAxis={{ dataKey: "week" }} series={[{ dataKey: "visits", label: seriesLabel, curveType: "linear", dot: true }]} height={190} showYAxis showLegend={false} />
    </Col>
    <Show.Else><DataTable columns={columns} rows={sessions} caption={tableCaption} /></Show.Else>
  </Show>
  <Text value={limitation} size="sm" color="secondary" />
  <Caption value={source} />
</Card>

data.demoNote: Illustrative museum attendance · six equal Saturday sessions
data.title: Visits rose from 120 to 180
data.takeaway: The last session had 60 more visits than the first (+50%), with a small dip in week 3.
data.tableCaption: All six sample counts; no sessions omitted.
data.limitation: The pattern alone cannot explain the rise. Opening hours are equal, but programming and weather are not controlled.
data.source: Source: synthetic gate-counter fixture; visits are entries, not unique people.
